rule_sets.py:328-333 `_binary` builds exp.Cast(this=node, to=exp.DataType.build("BINARY", dialect=_DIALECT)). sqlglot's MySQL parser yields DataType.Type.BINARY, which the MySQL generator leaves unmapped (its CAST_MAPPING only rewrites integer/other types to SIGNED etc.), so it renders CAST(x AS BINARY). In MySQL, the BINARY operator is documented as shorthand for CAST(expr AS BINARY), so the comparison is byte-wise and case/collation-sensitive. This rests on my knowledge of sqlglot and MySQL; I did not run sqlglot here. Used in _in_schema and _in_pairs (lines 336-347) as the claim describes.

rule_sets.py:150-153 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615" (2^64-1) with the quoted comment. Per the MySQL 8.0 manual, a derived table containing LIMIT cannot be merged into the outer query (the optimizer materializes it). Derived-condition pushdown (8.0.22+) is also not applied to a derived table with LIMIT. The manual's SELECT page gives 18446744073709551615 as the LIMIT value for 'all rows to the end', which is the unsigned 64-bit maximum. I checked the absolute wording against a query whose outer condition might still be pushed into the LIMIT-bearing derived table. The documented rules exclude that case, so I found no counterexample. I did not run MySQL, so this rests on documented behavior. The comment's claim that removing the LIMIT allows merge or pushdown is consistent with those rules.

rule_sets.py:535-558: apply_rule_set creates `expected` as a local dict (548) and passes it only to the two _rewalk calls (549, 557), with the same `tables` argument. `tables` is a parameter, so it stays referenced and alive for the whole call. CPython only reuses an id() after the object is freed, so id(tables) is unique among live objects and cannot collide with another set. The cache is not shared across calls: the only other caller, _rewalk's default (495), makes a fresh dict, and _is_catalog_derived is called only from _rewalk (503). Key (id(tables), view) at 479 therefore maps to one mapping for the call's lifetime. Text built for another set cannot be compared. The only way to break this is mutating `tables` mid-call, and no shipped caller does that; the call at 592 passes the runner's tables.

The code matches the claim's description. In rule_sets.py, `_is_catalog_derived` (482) compares `_generate(body)` with `expected[key]`, which is `_generate(_catalog_body(view, tables))`. `apply_rule_set` (549-557) runs `_rewalk` on the rewritten tree and again on the re-parsed output, using the same `expected` cache. `_catalog_body` (387-405) builds quoted identifiers, `CAST(... AS BINARY)`, `CurrentSchema()`, tuple IN lists and a paren-wrapped OR (350-384). Whether sqlglot's MySQL parser and generator reproduce that text exactly after a parse is a runtime property of the installed sqlglot version. Reading the source cannot settle it. Tests in tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py (373-386, 405-417) call `apply_rule_set` on the catalog views, so they would exercise the second re-walk. I did not run them (for example `pytest tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py`), and I have no output showing they pass. If the round trip were unstable, the failure would be a fail-closed refusal (KIND_UNCHECKED), not a bypass.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:110-148 defines _CATALOG_VIEWS with uppercase field names, and every `kept` name is a subset of `fields` (enforced at rule_sets.py:103). _catalog_body (rule_sets.py:387-405) projects fields in `spec.fields` order. tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:614-625 asserts pymysql.err.OperationalError for the unguarded query and len(frame)==0 for the guarded one. EXP(1000) raises MySQL error 1690 (DOUBLE value is out of range). pymysql's raise_mysql_exception maps only specific errnos to subclasses (1690 is not among them; WARN_DATA_OUT_OF_RANGE is 1264), and unmapped errnos of 1000 or higher fall back to OperationalError. I could not read the installed pymysql source (not in the views; pyproject.toml:57 only requires pymysql>=1.1), so that mapping is from knowledge of pymysql, not a read. src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:387-405 builds the catalog derived table with a WHERE filter on the allowed tables and a trailing LIMIT 18446744073709551615 (_MATERIALIZE_LIMIT, line 153). That forces materialization before the model's WHERE runs, so the rs_salaries row is never seen by EXP and the result is an empty frame. I did not run the test against a live MySQL.

MySQL runner (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:166-170) reads via SSDictCursor and calls rows_to_capped_df, which builds pd.DataFrame([dict(row)...]) (src/sqllens/safety/limits.py:70). SQL NULLs are None in the dicts, so the REFERENCED_* columns are object dtype holding None (or NaN if coerced). The test (tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:572-574) maps each value through `None if pd.isna(v) else v`. pd.isna is True for both None and NaN, so every NULL becomes None whatever the dtype. The expected tuples with None at 576-577 therefore compare equal. Non-null values stay strings, and the query has no duplicate column names. This was checked by reading the code. I did not run the test.
